articles.title: What makes rock deep beneath continents break away and sink?
articles.description: We usually picture mountain building as rock being pushed upward. But deep beneath some mountain belts and volcanic arcs, the opposite can happen: dense rock at the base of the crust can become unstable, break away and sink hundreds of kilometers into the mantle, dragging part of the rigid outer shell of the Earth (the lithosphere) with it.
